summary: Guo Jun is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA from Monash University and an MA from the University of Sydney, and studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute. Traditional teachers include Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin. He served as abbot of Singapore's Maha Bodhi Monastery.

Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Rissho University under Kenyo Mitomo. He studied under traditional teacher Sheng Yen and teachers including Hoyo Watanabe, Zensho Kitagawa, Gyoko Iotani, Seiichi Kiritani, Koken Sasaki, Zuiei Ito, and Kosuke Nakazawa.

Gurinder Singh Mann is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Baring Union Christian College, EFLU, Kent, Harvard, and Columbia (PhD). He taught at Baring Union, Columbia, and UC Santa Barbara, and founded the Global Institute for Sikh Studies.

id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga (1874–1957) was a Dutch religious studies scholar. He studied at Leiden University and held academic posts at Utrecht University (1924–1957) and the University of Amsterdam (1935–1944).

Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart, also studying with Hla Pe and John Okell. He served as a Senior Teaching Fellow in anthropology and sociology at SOAS.

Gustaf John Ramstedt (1873–1950) was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Helsinki, where he later held an academic post from circa 1901 to 1941, and worked at the University of Tokyo.

Gustav Haloun (1898–1951) was a sinologist who studied at Vienna, Leipzig (Dr. phil. under August Conrady), and Charles University. He held positions at Charles University, Halle-Wittenberg, and Göttingen, before serving as Chair of Chinese Language and History at Cambridge (1938–1951).

Gustav Hugo (1764–1844) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Göttingen and the University of Halle-Wittenberg, and held a long-standing academic post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1788 to 1844.

Gustav Mensching (1901–1978) worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Marburg, learning under Rudolf Otto. Mensching held academic posts at the University of Latvia (1927–1936) and the University of Bonn (1936).

Gustav Roth (1916–2008) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Breslau, Leipzig, Halle-Wittenberg, Munich (Dr. phil.), and Patna, learning under Paul Thieme among others. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, and ANU.

Gustav Salomon Oppert (1836–1908) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Bonn, Leipzig, and Halle-Wittenberg, as well as the Berlin University of the Arts, where he later held a post from circa 1895 to 1908.
Guus Kroonen is a linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky. He has held academic posts at the University of Copenhagen (circa 2013) and Leiden University (2016).

Guy Claxton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and learning sciences. He founded the Sharpham College for Buddhist Studies and Contemporary Enquiry and served as Professor of the Learning Sciences at the University of Bristol's Graduate School of Education.

Guy G. Stroumsa is a religious studies scholar educated at Paris, Hebrew University, EPHE, and Harvard (PhD). He was a faculty member at Hebrew University (which he also founded) and served as Professor of the Study of the Abrahamic Religions at Oxford.

Guy Newland is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, studied under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University.
Gyal Rong Tendzin Drakpa studied under the prominent teachers Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Patrul Rinpoche.

Gyatsho Tshering (1936–2009) was a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta. He founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, where he served as Acting Director in 1972 and Director from 1974 to 1998.

Gyoei Fukuda (1867–1954) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He served as president of Taisho University (~1926–1944), commissioned professor at the University of Tokyo (1928), and lecturer at Toyo University.

Gyoei Takahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held academic posts at Rissho University as assistant professor and professor. Takahashi also served as a member of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra.
Gyoin Hashimoto (1897–1978) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Join Saeki. He served as the head priest (kanji) of Yakushi-ji from 1939 to 1967.
